description:
FOUND s501b (Opus, 2026-09-30) answering #2083's second question by measurement.  PRE-EXISTING.

PROBES (scratch/s501b/p/rec1.pl, rec2.pl in the s501b worktree):
    my $n = 0; sub f { $n++; f() } eval { f() }; print "trapped: ", ($@ ? "yes" : "no"), "\n";
    our $d = 0; sub g { local $d = $d + 1; g() } eval { g() }; print "trapped: ", ($@ ? "yes" : "no"), "\n";
PCL (both): "INFO: Binding stack guard page unprotected / Binding stack guard page temporarily disabled: proceed with caution / While evaluating the form starting at line N ... Unhandled sb-kernel::binding-stack-exhausted ..." followed by a multi-hundred-line Lisp backtrace; the eval does NOT trap it; `trapped:` never prints.
perl: neither is trappable either -- perl has no recursion limit; the process grows until "Out of memory!" (and prints "Deep recursion" warnings under `use warnings`).  So the DIVERGENCE is not trappability but the FORM: the USER rule (s494) is that an error fails in the same place as perl and is TIDY -- one line, never a Lisp backtrace.

The binding stack (special bindings: every `local`, every p-sub frame's *wantarray*/caller bindings) runs out long before the 512 MB control stack; Math::BigFloat's #2083 infinite recursion (an isa override calling UNIVERSAL::isa) showed it as 300+ identical frames.

CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT: does the control-stack guard (sb-kernel::control-stack-exhausted) already get a tidy handler somewhere in the runtime's toplevel (grep `control-stack-exhausted` in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp)?  If yes, the fix is to route binding-stack-exhausted (and heap-exhausted) through the same one-line reporter ("Out of memory!" / "Deep recursion ..." shaped, exit status as perl's).  Also measure whether --binding-stack-size is set by tools/lib/PCLSbcl.pm.

BAR: runtime-only; a Pl/t row asserting stderr is ONE line and the exit status is nonzero.
subject: A runaway recursion ends as a raw SBCL "Binding stack exhausted" abort with a Lisp backtrace (not one tidy line); perl runs until "Out of memory!"
